items.stem: A circle is inscribed in a ΔABC touching AB, BC and AC at P, Q and R respectively. If AB = 10 cm, AR = 7 cm and CR = 5 cm, then find the length of BC.
items.answer: Tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are equal in length. From A, AP = AR = 7 cm. From C, CQ = CR = 5 cm. Hence BP = AB − AP = 10 − 7 = 3 cm, and from B, BQ = BP = 3 cm. Therefore BC = BQ + QC = 3 + 5 = 8 cm.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point
items.section_heading: TWO MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Basic

items.stem: Prove that in two concentric circles, the chord of the larger circle, which touches the smaller circle is bisected at the point of contact.
items.answer: Let the two circles have the common centre O, and let AB be a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle at P. OP is a radius of the smaller circle and AB is a tangent to it at P, so OP ⊥ AB. Now for the larger circle O is the centre and AB is a chord with OP ⊥ AB, and the perpendicular drawn from the centre to a chord bisects the chord. Hence AP = PB, that is, the chord is bisected at the point of contact. Hence proved.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: In figure, a circle touches all the four sides of a quadrilateral ABCD. If AB = 6 cm, BC = 9 cm and CD = 8 cm, then find the length of AD.
items.answer: Let the circle touch AB, BC, CD and DA at P, Q, R and S respectively. Tangents from an external point are equal, so let AP = AS = x. Then BP = AB − AP = 6 − x and BQ = BP = 6 − x. Next CQ = BC − BQ = 9 − (6 − x) = 3 + x and CR = CQ = 3 + x. Then RD = CD − CR = 8 − (3 + x) = 5 − x and DS = RD = 5 − x. Therefore AD = AS + SD = x + (5 − x) = 5. Thus AD = 5 cm.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point

items.stem: In the given figure, from a point P, two tangents PT and PS are drawn to a circle with centre O such that ∠SPT = 120°. Prove that OP = 2PS.
items.answer: PT and PS are equal tangents from P, so OP bisects ∠SPT and ∠OPS = 120° ÷ 2 = 60°. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠OSP = 90° and triangle POS is right angled at S. In that triangle cos 60° = PS/OP, that is ½ = PS/OP. Therefore OP = 2PS. Hence proved.

items.stem: From an external point P, tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O. If ∠PAB = 50°, then find ∠AOB.
items.answer: PA is a tangent and OA is the radius to its point of contact, so PA ⊥ OA and ∠OAP = 90°. Hence ∠OAB = ∠OAP − ∠BAP = 90° − 50° = 40°. OA and OB are radii of the same circle, so triangle OAB is isosceles and ∠OBA = ∠OAB = 40°. By the angle sum property ∠AOB + 40° + 40° = 180°. Therefore ∠AOB = 100°.

items.stem: In given figure, AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O and AT is a tangent. If ∠AOQ = 58°, find ∠ATQ.
items.answer: ∠ABQ and ∠AOQ stand on the same arc AQ, the first at the circumference and the second at the centre, so ∠ABQ = ½ × 58° = 29°. OA is a radius and TA is the tangent at A, so OA ⊥ TA and ∠BAT = 90°. In triangle BAT, ∠ATB = 90° − ∠ABT = 90° − 29° = 61°. Therefore ∠ATQ = ∠ATB = 61°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: Prove that the lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
items.answer: Let the circle have centre O and radius r, and let two tangents from an external point P touch it at A and B. Join OA, OB and OP. In triangles PAO and PBO, OP is common and OA = OB = r, being radii of the same circle. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° and both triangles are right angled. By the RHS congruence rule ΔPAO ≅ ΔPBO, and hence AP = BP. Thus the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the given figure PQ is chord of length 6 cm of the circle of radius 6 cm. TP and TQ are tangents to the circle at points P and Q respectively. Find ∠PTQ.
items.answer: Here PQ = 6 cm and OP = OQ = 6 cm, the radius, so triangle PQO has all three sides equal and is equilateral. Hence ∠POQ = 60°. Since OP ⊥ TP and OQ ⊥ TQ, the angles ∠POQ and ∠PTQ of quadrilateral OPTQ are supplementary, so ∠PTQ = 180° − 60° = 120°.

items.stem: In figure, two tangents RQ and RP are drawn from an external point R to the circle with centre O. If ∠PRQ = 120°, then prove that OR = PR + RQ.
items.answer: Join O to P. RP and RQ are equal tangents from R, so OR bisects ∠PRQ and ∠PRO = ½ × 120° = 60°. OP ⊥ RP because a radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so triangle OPR is right angled at P and ∠POR = 90° − 60° = 30°. Then PR/OR = sin 30° = ½, so OR = 2PR = PR + PR. Since PR = QR, being equal tangents from R, OR = PR + RQ. Hence proved.

items.stem: In figure, O is the centre of a circle. PT are tangents to the circle from an external point P. If ∠TPQ = 70°, find ∠TRQ.
items.answer: Join O to T and to Q. PT and PQ are tangents, so OT ⊥ PT and OQ ⊥ PQ, and hence ∠TOQ and ∠TPQ are supplementary. Thus ∠TOQ = 180° − 70° = 110°. Now ∠TRQ and ∠TOQ stand on the same arc TQ, the first at the circumference and the second at the centre, so ∠TRQ = ½ × 110° = 55°.

items.stem: Prove that tangents drawn at the ends of a chord of a circle make equal angles with the chord.
items.answer: Let MN be a chord of the circle and let the tangents at M and N meet at the external point P. The two tangents from P are equal, so PM = PN. In triangle PMN the angles opposite these equal sides are equal, so ∠1 = ∠2, where ∠1 and ∠2 are the angles the tangents make with the chord on the side of P. The angles ∠3 and ∠4 on the other side of the chord form linear pairs with ∠1 and ∠2, so 180° − ∠1 = 180° − ∠2 gives ∠3 = ∠4. Hence the tangents at the ends of a chord make equal angles with the chord. Hence proved.

items.stem: In Figure a quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle, with centre O, in such a way that the sides AB, BC, CD and DA touch the circle at the points P, Q, R and S respectively. Prove that AB + CD = BC + DA.
items.answer: Tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are equal in length, so at A, AP = AS; at B, BP = BQ; at C, CR = CQ; and at D, DR = DS. Adding these four results gives AP + BP + DR + CR = AS + DS + BQ + CQ. Regrouping, (AP + PB) + (CR + RD) = (AS + SD) + (BQ + QC), that is AB + CD = AD + BC. Hence AB + CD = BC + DA. Hence proved.

items.stem: In Figure, common tangents AB and CD to the two circle with centres O₁ and O₂ intersect at E. Prove that AB = CD.
items.answer: EA and EC are tangents drawn from the point E to the circle with centre O₁, so EA = EC. Likewise EB and ED are tangents from E to the circle with centre O₂, so EB = ED. Adding the two gives EA + EB = EC + ED. Since E lies between A and B on one common tangent and between C and D on the other, EA + EB = AB and EC + ED = CD. Therefore AB = CD. Hence proved.

items.stem: Two tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle inclined to each other at an angle of 70°, then what is the value of ∠PAB?
items.answer: In quadrilateral OAPB the angles ∠AOB and ∠APB are supplementary, so ∠AOB = 180° − 70° = 110°. OA and OB are radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles with ∠OAB = ∠OBA, and from the angle sum 2∠OAB = 180° − 110° = 70°, giving ∠OAB = 35°. OA is a radius and AP is the tangent at A, so OA ⊥ AP and ∠OAP = 90°. Therefore ∠PAB = ∠OAP − ∠OAB = 90° − 35° = 55°.

items.stem: In the given figure, BOA is a diameter of a circle and the tangent at a point P meets BA when produced at T. If ∠PBO = 30°, what is the measure of ∠PTA?
items.answer: An angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle, so ∠BPA = 90°. OB and OP are radii, so triangle OBP is isosceles and ∠BPO = ∠PBO = 30°. The exterior angle at O gives ∠POA = ∠OBP + ∠OPB = 30° + 30° = 60°, so ∠POT = 60°. OP is a radius and PT is the tangent at P, so OP ⊥ PT and ∠OPT = 90°. In triangle OPT, ∠PTO = 180° − (90° + 60°) = 30°. Therefore ∠PTA = ∠PTO = 30°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: In figure, O is the centre of the circle and LN is a diameter. If PQ is a tangent to the circle at K and ∠KLN = 30°, find ∠PKL.
items.answer: OK and OL are radii of the circle, so OK = OL and triangle OKL is isosceles. The angles opposite the equal sides are equal, so ∠OKL = ∠OLK = 30°. PQ is the tangent at K and OK is the radius to the point of contact, so OK ⊥ PQ and ∠OKP = 90°. Therefore ∠PKL = ∠OKP − ∠OKL = 90° − 30° = 60°.
items.concept: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius

items.stem: In the given figure, if AB = AC, prove that BE = CE.
items.answer: The inscribed circle touches AB at D, BC at E and AC at F. Tangents from an external point are equal, so AD = AF, BD = BE and CE = CF. Given AB = AC, we have AD + DB = AF + FC, and since AD = AF this leaves DB = FC. Substituting BD = BE and CF = CE gives BE = CE. Hence proved.
